reason: This passage from 1 Kings 17-18 describes Elijah's confrontation with King Ahab and the prophets of Baal, culminating in the test on Mount Carmel. While Elijah does address the Israelite people directly (asking how long they will waver between two opinions), and Ahab accuses Elijah of troubling Israel, neither Elijah nor other Hebrew leaders lodge complaints about the people's conduct. The narrative focuses on prophetic confrontation and divine vindication rather than leaders complaining about the populace.
